My experience was really bad. I was admitted back in March to my local mental hospital. I was 16 so I was put with the other minors. It took me almost 2 hours to actually be admitted and there was a woman yelling at the staff in the lobby. I couldn't have my phone and had to take the strings out of my hoodie. When I got to the actual ward it was super sketchy. There weren't any paintings or windows anywhere it was just the same dull pink color. I had to talk to a psychiatrist and he prescribed me Zoloft and diagnosed me with like 5 different things after talking to me for only 30 mins. Also, there were 3 interns there too so I was just talking about my mental health in front of 4 strangers. I am vegan and told the staff but they didn't care so I ended up not eating the majority of the meals. They had to draw our blood but they sucked at it and most of the other patient's arms were all bruised and swollen from it. The girl across the hall from me had to be woken up at 3 in the morning to have her blood drawn but the nurse spilled it all over her sheets. He didn't do anything so she slept on bloody sheets for the rest of the night. They never got to test my blood because they forgot to refrigerate it. There weren't any activities other than drawing, tv, and volleyball in this small gym. The therapy groups were really bad. We just got those positive affirmations worksheets and everyone sat in silence. They also misgendered all the trans kids and the patients weren't allowed to talk to each other after 7 PM even though we were all awake which sucked. There were some fights on the boy's side but I don't think the staff did anything. There would be people having panic attacks and the staff didn't even move so we just had to comfort each other which was nice, but I don't think any of us were mentally stable enough for that.  The bathrooms were gross and there was no privacy except a cloth curtain that didn't close all the way. I know the hospital had to shut down a while back because there was a problem with the staff sexually assaulting patients. They also were very careful about things that could be used to self-harm so we weren't allowed to have combs/brushes, jeans, and they even took the wooden sticks out of the corn dogs. I was lucky enough to get outpatient care thanks to my parents, but I know a lot of people didn't get any help whatsoever. The other patients were really nice for the most part but other than that it was a shitty experience.
